text:
Maria Chen: quick heads-up — ran the group-size sweep (group_sizes 16/32/64) on the 8k-seqlen mixed workload with AWQ and GPTQ calibrated checkpoints. Observed a 12-18% p99 latency regression when group_size=64 and packing is enabled (dedupe+prefetch on). perf-bot uploaded the trace: perf-bot:uploaded:2432109876.trace

Liam Patel: can you drop the profile snippets? need kernel dispatch/hotpath info. is the kernel chooser flipping to a fallback?

Maria Chen: here's the short grep from the runtime trace — kernel dispatch counts and latency buckets:
```
kernel:int8_group64_specialized - calls: 432 - avg_ms:0.82 - p99_ms:2.1
kernel:int8_generic - calls: 120 - avg_ms:1.9 - p99_ms:4.8
packing:dedupe_hits:312 - unpack_calls:58 - packing_overhead_ms_total:1234
kvcache:evictions:482 - spill_io_ms:920
```

Aisha Gomez: hypothesis: when packer coalesces buffers for group_size=64 we cross an internal stride boundary and the kernel chooser prefers the generic int8 matmul (worse perf). Also packing dedupe/unpack adds extra GPU copies for that group alignment. Might be a packing-alignment -> kernel-mismatch cascade.

Noah Rivera: adding that KV cache eviction number is concerning — pack-induced buffer size variance can increase KV writes and force spill. Seen similar in staging when we had unaligned slab sizes. Patch that aligns pack buffers to 256B helped before.

Liam Patel: I'll run a quick A/B: baseline (packing on) vs pack-aligned patch (align to 256) vs forcing specialized int8 kernel (override chooser) for group64. Results in ~30min.

perf-bot:deploy:triggered - profile job queued (job 2432109876-xfer)

Liam Patel: quick results (batch=32, mix of short+long requests):
```
baseline (pack on): p50 14ms p95 78ms p99 152ms tokens/s 420
pack-align-256: p50 13ms p95 72ms p99 142ms tokens/s 438
force-int8-specialized: p50 13ms p95 66ms p99 126ms tokens/s 462
KV evictions baseline 482 -> align 410 -> force 218
Quality (eval set) AWQ: ppl delta +0.6% (pack-align), +0.9% (force-specialized)
```

Maria Chen: interesting — forcing the specialized kernel gives the clearest p99 win and cuts KV evictions a lot. small quality hit but within rollback threshold.

Aisha Gomez: two options: 1) make kernel-chooser prefer specialized-int8 for group_size>=48 when packing pattern matches (cheap rule), or 2) change packer to avoid formation of the problematic alignments (costly rewrite). I prefer (1) as a short-term fix.

Noah Rivera: short-term (1) is fine, but we should still fix packer alignment long-term to reduce memory churn. I'll open a follow-up for allocator alignment + unit tests for slab boundaries.

Liam Patel: filed canary PR that flips chooser heuristic: runtime/chooser: prefer int8_specialized when (group>=48 && pack_stride % 256 == 0). Ran canary on dedicated pool: p99 improved ~16% vs baseline, deploy looks green. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3456

Maria Chen: nice. let's ship heuristic + telemetry to track kernel fallback counts (new metric: kernel_chooser_fallbacks). Also add a perf regression alert for p99 > +10% vs baseline.

perf-bot:metric:registered kernel_chooser_fallbacks

Aisha Gomez: also add a small microbench for packing overhead in CI (pack/unpack timings for group sizes 16/32/64). Cc @eng-runtime.

Noah Rivera: follow-up tasks: (a) allocator alignment patch (b) pack dedupe perf test (c) telemetry dashboard for pack/unpack and kernel dispatch heatmap. I'll put them in the sprint board.

Maria Chen: thanks all — action items captured. outcome: short-term chooser heuristic reduces p99 and KV eviction; medium-term packer/allocator work to remove source cause. :thumbsup:
